_about: Deliberate changes to the call contract of tools that are on master. Each entry needs a real benefit and what a caller must change. tests/test_backward_compat.py fails on any undeclared change, and on any entry here that no longer matches a detected change. Kinds: removed_tool, removed_parameter, new_required_parameter, default_changed (all detected automatically), and behaviour (a change the signature does not show, such as stricter validation or a changed response field; not detected, so declare it by hand). A behaviour entry may use tool "*" when the change applies to every tool on master.

changes.what_changed: An id that contains a slash, a question mark, a hash, two dots in a row or a space is now refused before any request is sent. Before, such an id was placed in the request address as written, so get_creative('123/') read creative 123 and an id like '123/ads' read a different object than the tool was meant to read.
changes.why_better: A tool can only reach the object type it was built for. An id copied from text that strangers wrote (an ad comment, a Page review) can no longer steer a read or a delete to a different object or attach extra options to the request.
changes.migration: Pass the plain id with nothing before or after it, for example '123' or 'act_123'. Trim a trailing slash or any address fragment before calling.

changes.what_changed: file_path is now read only from the one folder named by the META_UPLOAD_DIR environment variable, the same rule every other upload tool follows. A path outside that folder, a link inside it that points outside, a file that is not .jpg, .jpeg or .png, an empty file and a file over 30 MB are refused before anything is sent to Meta, and every local path is refused while META_UPLOAD_DIR is unset. Before, any file anywhere on the machine was read and sent to Meta, whatever its type or size. The request sent for an accepted file is unchanged, and image_url calls are unchanged.
changes.why_better: The model that calls this tool also reads text written by strangers, such as ad comments and Page reviews. Before, a path slipped into that text could make the tool send any private file on your computer, such as a key or a document, to a Meta ad account. Now only images you have put in your chosen upload folder can ever leave the machine, and a wrong path gets a clear message that never repeats the path.
changes.migration: Set META_UPLOAD_DIR in the server's environment to one folder, put the images to upload there, and pass a path inside that folder or a file name relative to it. Use .jpg, .jpeg or .png files of at most 30 MB. Calls that pass image_url need no change.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap inside params is now refused before any request is sent, with a message pointing to the named spend_cap parameter. Before, params={'spend_cap': 25000} was sent to Meta as written and read in minor units (250.00 USD), while the named spend_cap takes major units (spend_cap=250 is 250.00). daily_budget and lifetime_budget inside params were already refused; only their message changed.
changes.why_better: The same field no longer has two units, so an amount cannot silently be 100 times too small (or too large) because it was put in params instead of the named parameter.
changes.migration: Move the amount to the named spend_cap parameter in major units: divide the minor-unit amount you sent in params by the currency's minor-unit factor, 100 for most currencies and 1 for currencies without minor units such as JPY or KRW. params={'spend_cap': 25000} in USD becomes spend_cap=250.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap inside params is now refused before any request is sent, including the read of the campaign, with a message pointing to the named spend_cap parameter. Before, params={'spend_cap': 25000} was sent to Meta as written and read in minor units (250.00 USD), while the named spend_cap takes major units. daily_budget and lifetime_budget inside params were already refused; only their message changed.
changes.why_better: The same field no longer has two units, so an amount cannot silently be 100 times too small (or too large) because it was put in params instead of the named parameter.
changes.migration: Move the amount to the named spend_cap parameter in major units: divide the minor-unit amount you sent in params by the currency's minor-unit factor, 100 for most currencies and 1 for currencies without minor units such as JPY or KRW. params={'spend_cap': 25000} in USD becomes spend_cap=250.

changes.what_changed: daily_spend_cap, lifetime_spend_cap, daily_min_spend_target and lifetime_min_spend_target inside params are now refused before any request is sent, with a message pointing to the named parameter of the same name. Before, they were sent to Meta as written and read in minor units, while the named parameters take major units. bid_amount, daily_budget and lifetime_budget inside params were already refused; only their message changed.
changes.why_better: The same field no longer has two units, so an amount cannot silently be 100 times too small (or too large) because it was put in params instead of the named parameter.
changes.migration: Move each amount to the named parameter of the same name in major units: divide the minor-unit amount you sent in params by the currency's minor-unit factor, 100 for most currencies and 1 for currencies without minor units such as JPY or KRW. params={'daily_spend_cap': 9000} in USD becomes daily_spend_cap=90.

changes.what_changed: When a call changes the audience rule, whether through the named rule parameter or through params={'rule': ...}, the tool now also asks Meta for the audience's current rule in the read it already makes before updating, and returns it as previous.rule. Before, a params-only rule change read and returned the other fields but not the old rule.
changes.why_better: The rule decides who is in the audience, and Meta does not keep the old one. Returning it before it is replaced is the only way to put it back if the new rule turns out to be wrong.
changes.migration: No change to how the tool is called. The response has one more field, previous.rule; the read before the update asks for one more field.
